the-christian-who-moved-to-south-africa.excerpt: The Christian who has moved to South Africa in the last year — for work, for family, for safety — is still in the adjustment phase. Here is what the Bible says about the new arrival, the strange land, and the long road of integration.

the-foreign-christian-in-south-africa.title: The Christian From Zimbabwe, Malawi, and Mozambique in Johannesburg: A Bible Study on the Stranger in the City of Gold
the-foreign-christian-in-south-africa.excerpt: The Christian from Harare, Lilongwe, or Maputo who is working in Johannesburg is one of the most faithful members of South African church life. They tithe faithfully. They serve enthusiastically. They are also some of the most vulnerable people in the city. Here is what the Bible says about the stranger, and how the Johannesburg church is failing and can be rebuilt.

the-neighbourhood-watch-and-the-christia.title: The Neighbourhood Watch and the Christian: A South African's Guide to Community Safety, Vigilantism, and Doing Good Without Becoming What You Fear
the-neighbourhood-watch-and-the-christia.excerpt: The Christian in the Johannesburg neighbourhood watch faces a specific moral challenge. The crime is real. The fear is legitimate. The response needs to be proportional. Here is what the Bible says about justice, community safety, and the difference between protecting your neighbours and becoming what you are protecting them from.

the-single-christian-mother-in-sandton.title: The Single Christian Mother in Sandton: A South African's Honest Guide to Raising Children Alone and Faithfully
the-single-christian-mother-in-sandton.excerpt: The single Christian mother in Johannesburg carries two loads — the load of parenting alone and the load of faith in a God who sometimes feels far away. The school runs, the rent, the taxi fare, the homework, the bedtime — all of it falls on one pair of shoulders. Here is what the Bible says about the single mother, and how the Wednesday Bible study in Parkmore has learned to hold her.

the-south-african-christian-and-the-divo.title: After the Divorce: A South African Christian's Honest Guide to the Years That Follow the Broken Vow
the-south-african-christian-and-the-divo.excerpt: The Christian in South Africa who has been through a divorce carries a particular burden. The Bible is clear that marriage is a covenant. The Bible is also clear that God is near to the broken heart.

the-teacher-who-is-also-a-christian.title: Teaching in Jesus' Name: A South African Christian Teacher's Honest Guide to Faith, Pedagogy, and the Classroom as a Mission Field
the-teacher-who-is-also-a-christian.excerpt: The Christian teacher in Johannesburg — in the government school, the private school, or the independent school — carries a specific calling. Here is what the Bible says about teaching, influence, and the classroom as a place of witness.

the-widower-in-johannesburg.title: The Widower in Johannesburg: A South African Christian's Honest Guide to Being a Man Alone After Your Wife Has Died
the-widower-in-johannesburg.excerpt: The widower in Johannesburg faces a particular loneliness that the church rarely addresses. The widower is not single. He was married for thirty years. He does not know how to cook. He does not know how to shop. He does not know how to be alone. Here is what the Bible says about the widower, and how the church can do better.

time-management-for-the-busy-christian.title: There Are Only Twenty-Four Hours: A South African Christian's Honest Guide to Time Management, Sabbath Rest, and the Discipline of Doing Less
time-management-for-the-busy-christian.excerpt: The Christian in Johannesburg in 2026 is busier than ever. The job, the children, the church, the community obligations, the WhatsApp groups, the traffic, the load-shedding. There is never enough time. Here is what the Bible says about time, rest, and the discipline of doing less.

traffic-and-the-christian-driver.title: In Traffic on the N1: A South African Christian's Honest Guide to Road Rage, Patience, and the Theology of the Morning Commute
traffic-and-the-christian-driver.excerpt: The Christian driver in Johannesburg faces a daily test of character that the Bible addresses directly. The N1 traffic, the taxis that do not indicate, the driver who cut you off, the moment when the anger takes over and the words come out of the mouth. Here is what the Bible says about traffic and how to survive it faithfully.

volunteering-burnout.title: The Volunteer Who Does Everything: A South African Christian's Honest Guide to Church Volunteering, Burnout, and Saying No to Good Things
volunteering-burnout.excerpt: The Christian in Johannesburg who volunteers for everything — the braai setup, the worship team, the youth group, the welcoming committee, the pastoral care visits — is doing good things. They are also heading for a fall. Here is what the Bible says about volunteer burnout.

when-the-language-changes-in-church.title: When the Church Changes the Language: A South African Christian's Guide to Congregational Language Shift and the God Who Speaks Every Language
when-the-language-changes-in-church.excerpt: The church in Johannesburg that has shifted from one language to another — from English to Zulu, from Afrikaans to English, from Sotho to multilingual — creates both grief and opportunity. Here is what the Bible says about language in worship.

when-the-pastor-quits.title: When the Pastor Resigns: A South African Christian's Honest Guide to Leadership Transitions, Grief, and the God Who Is Still in Charge
when-the-pastor-quits.excerpt: The Christian in Johannesburg whose pastor has resigned — for reasons good or bad — faces a specific kind of community grief. Here is what the Bible says about leadership transitions and how to navigate them with faith.
